pre_f0_candidates.title: The Intervention Knowledge Bottleneck: Convergent Failure at Entity-Level Modification Knowledge
pre_f0_candidates.irreducible_object: The structural constraint that makes entity-level intervention knowledge (how to change specific code entities) a convergent failure point for both repository-grounded skill distillation and interaction-feedback skill evolution, despite their different knowledge acquisition mechanisms.

P.label: principle_or_problem_formulation
P.rationale: The problem of identifying a convergent failure point across independent method families is formulated, but requires validation that the convergence is not coincidental or reducible to a generic limitation in knowledge acquisition.

M.label: method_or_method_boundary
M.rationale: No new method is proposed; the contribution is the identification and characterization of the convergent failure regime.

E.label: empirical_phenomenon
E.rationale: The empirical evidence from two independent methods (SkillForge and SkillEvo) shows convergent failure at the intervention knowledge level, satisfying the lane contract for convergent failure.

T.label: theory_or_guarantee
T.rationale: A theoretical contribution is possible if the structural constraint causing the convergence can be formalized (e.g., as a fundamental limitation in representing actionable modification knowledge), but this requires showing the constraint is not already captured by existing theories of knowledge representation or acquisition.

S.label: system_or_capability
S.rationale: No new system capability is claimed.

pre_f0_candidates.exact_prediction: Across additional independent self-evolution methods (beyond SkillForge and SkillEvo), failure will consistently occur at the entity-level intervention knowledge level when the acquisition mechanism lacks multi-turn interaction or entity-grounded modification examples, and this failure will not be overcome by simply increasing the quantity of single-turn or non-entity-grounded data.
pre_f0_candidates.strongest_same_information_baseline: Knowledge representation bottleneck theory (procedural vs declarative knowledge) applied to self-evolving agents.
pre_f0_candidates.cheapest_problem_falsifier: Identify a third independent self-evolution method (e.g., a different knowledge acquisition approach) and test whether it also fails specifically at entity-level intervention knowledge when lacking multi-turn or entity-grounded data. If the third method does not show this convergent failure, or if the failure is overcome by increasing data quantity without the specific structural characteristics, the convergence claim is falsified.
pre_f0_candidates.endpoint_headroom_requirement: The convergent failure must be observed in at least one additional independent method with a statistically significant performance drop (e.g., >3%) at the intervention knowledge level, and the failure must persist despite increased data quantity lacking the required structural characteristics.
